1.       Recommendation

For information.

2.       Purpose / Issue:

The purpose of this report is to provide an update on construction timelines and
progress of the Kitchener Central Transit Hub (KCTH).

3.       Strategic Plan:

The Kitchener Central Transit Hub will demonstrate the Region of Waterloo’s
commitment to sustainable transportation and supports each strategic priority of our
“Growing with Care” Strategic Plan:

         Homes for All: An enhanced transportation network and travel options support
          affordable housing developments throughout the Waterloo Region and opens
          broader employment opportunities.

         Climate-aligned Growth: Increased transit and active transportation options
          help facilitate user choice, make life more affordable and achieve climate action
          goals.

         Equitable Services and Opportunities: Increased access to transportation
          options helps unlock new opportunities for residents throughout Waterloo
          Region.

         Resilient and Future Ready Organization: The new transit hub will provide
          improved access to affordable transportation options that support future growth in
          our community.

5.       Background:

The Kitchener Central Transit Hub (KCTH) is a transformational project involving
Metrolinx, Region of Waterloo, City of Kitchener and several other stakeholders focused
on delivering an integrated transit network for the area.

Building off the success of ION light rail, KCTH is a project that will show Waterloo
Region’s commitment to sustainable transportation and spur economic development in
the area. It will also support future planned light rail expansion to Cambridge.

KCTH will connect residents and visitors to the Toronto-Waterloo innovation corridor by
providing access to Grand River Transit light rail and bus service, GO Transit rail and
bus service, VIA Rail and allow for inter-city bus service. The new transit hub will
integrate active transportation options with separated cycling and pedestrian paths and
include transit priority lanes.

Project Updates

Design work for the KCTH building and related projects is continuing, with the Region
focused on completing the design by the end of 2026 while also working to secure
required approvals. The Region is also working closely with Metrolinx to confirm the
construction schedule. Once Metrolinx’s contractor is in place, a coordinated project
schedule will be finalized.

The Region has retained PCL as Construction Manager to support preconstruction
work. Preliminary reviews of the early design are complete, with input provided on
constructability, cost effectiveness, scheduling, and staging to help advance project
delivery.

Region staff are partnering with ENOVA and Metrolinx to bury the hydro lines along
Waterloo Street between Breithaupt and King Street, which currently cross over the rail
corridor. This work is expected to commence in 2026, with completion prior to
Metrolinx’s construction work beginning.

After that work is complete, construction is planned to begin in 2026, starting with
demolition of the non-heritage section of the Rumpel Felt building. The transit hub and
related site works are targeted for completion by the end of 2031.

Corresponding Projects

Rumpel Felt Partial Demolition

The Region has received approval from the City of Kitchener to demolish the non-
heritage building elements to accommodate the turning radius required for transit
providers to enter and exit the bus loop off Duke St. and allow for a pick-up and drop-off
for KCTH.

Approval from Canadian Wildlife Services is still required concerning modifications to
the existing chimney. The Region is working with this agency to confirm the preferred
approach to preserving the Chimney Swift habitat.

Staff are exploring potential future uses for the retained portion of the Rumpel Felt
building, including opportunities for adaptive reuse or revitalisation. As part of this

Victoria Street Modifications (King Street West to Weber Street West)

This project includes modifications to Victoria Street between King Street and Weber
Street to provide multimodal links to KCTH. A preliminary design has been approved by
Council in December 2024 (TSD-TRP-24-019) which includes a reduction from four
vehicle lanes to two vehicle lanes to allow for new transit priority lanes and active
transportation infrastructure.

Coordination between project teams is underway to align construction timelines and
integrated elements. Discussions with utilities such as Enova Power, Bell, and
Kitchener Utilities is also underway, with utility relocations projected for summer of
2026. Design is expected to be completed shortly with tender to go out in September
2026 and construction expected in 2027.

Budgetary and Agreement Updates

The Region is delivering KCTH through two funding agreements. The first is with the
Ministry of Transportation and provides up to $33 million for Phase 1 work, including the
pedestrian bridge and ramp. The second is through the Investing in Canada
Infrastructure Program, under the Public Transit stream, and provides $93 million in
federal and provincial funding. This funding supports construction of the transit hub,
expansion of the bus loop, and development of the pedestrian plaza at King and Victoria
streets.

The Region is working to keep the project within budget. To help manage costs, value
engineering work has been completed with support from the Region’s Construction
Manager to identify savings and reduce the risk of cost overruns.

6.   Communication and Engagement with Area Municipalities and the Public

Area Municipalities:
The Region has been working with City of Kitchener staff on several parts of the project,
including the multi-use trail design, ownership of Duke Street, and related utilities. The
Region and the City are also reviewing stormwater management for the site and
surrounding area and will be discussing public art selection in the transit hub atrium.

As part of the design process, the Region completed a pre-submission meeting with the
City. This provided helpful feedback on zoning, site access, parking, landscape design,
and heritage requirements, which is helping to inform the next stages of design.

Public:
To improve coordination across organizations, the Region has initiated quarterly
communications meetings with Metrolinx. These meetings are intended to align timing,
messaging, and public notices for work in the KCTH area. Where Metrolinx construction

The 2026-2035 Facilities and Fleet Capital Program includes a budget of $35 million for
the Kitchener Central Transit Hub Project Phase 1; of which $2.23 million is allocated to
2026. The project is funded as follows: $33 million from the Provincial government
(MTO) and regionally through $0.8 million RDC debenture and $1.2 million levy
supported debentures. Of the $33 million, $4.9 million has been consumed to date.

The 2026-2035 Facilities and Fleet Capital Program includes a budget of $129 million
for the Kitchener Central Transit Hub Project Phase 2; of which $3.3 million is allocated
to 2026. The project is funded as follows: $42 million from the Provincial government
(MTO), $52 million from the Federal government and regionally through $14 million
RDC debenture, $21 million through levy supported debentures. Of the $94 million
government funding, $1.2 million has been consumed to date.
